To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the benefit of buying from the local market depends on where the consumer lives, the benefit of buying online depends on how close the consumer is to the online retailer, and the benefit of buying offline depends on how close consumers are to the local retailer.
the benefit of buying online depends on where you live, and the benefit of buying in a store depends on how far away it is.

1) consumers are more sensitive to online price discounts when a local retail store is not present, 2) consumers are less sensitive to online price when a store opens, and 3) consumers are less likely to buy online when a store opens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the determinants of consumer choice between local retail stores and online retailers.
how a consumer’s physical environment affects his/her online purchases.
the interaction of the online and offline worlds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
consumers are more likely to buy online when the local retail market is more competitive, and less likely to buy online as the online price discount increases.
the benefit of buying online depends on where you live.
the benefit of buying online depends on the local market conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the parameters in many existing theoretical models of consumer channel substitution interact in a way that determines consumer choice of channels.
consumers are willing to pay a premium to buy locally, but only if it is convenient to do so.
the benefits of buying locally are not trivial and that the disutility of buying online can be substantial, especially when a consumer lives in an area with many local stores.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the benefits of buying from local stores depend on the costs of buying online, which are a function of both transportation and disutility costs.
consumers’ physical location is a key determinant of their channel choices, and that the parameters in theoretical models of channel choice are empirically relevant.
consumers’ location is important for understanding the relative benefits of purchasing from the online versus the local world.
